title: Consolidated Exemption API Backdoor (Legacy Conversion Bypass)
pattern: A dedicated function or wrapper designed to bypass safety or security boundaries, created to avoid rewriting legacy callers that do not conform to modern type/conformance constraints.
why_bad: Permanent vulnerabilities. It consolidates "escape hatches" and serves as a permanent architectural backdoor. Unconstrained by automated linters, developers naturally default to utilizing these easy-to-use bypasses instead of undertaking the hard work of migrating callers to type-safe interfaces.
detection:
The linter must observe:
1. A function containing bypass terminology (e.g., `unsafe_legacy`, `untrusted_sql`, `legacy_convert`) in its name.
2. The function is invoked by newly added code paths or is not restricted by visibility rules (like build-system whitelists or restricted compiler annotations).
source: - Heather Adkins et al., *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (2020) [32, 558]
